mutations.because: The lane's whole claim, on the column side: the switch is over the middle column, so it must CHANGE the middle column. This is the shape the half-migration takes when the buttons are moved and the swap is not -- and it is the plausible version, not a random deletion, because `columnPanels.editor` is what the column rendered for its entire life before this lane and reads as the safe default. Nothing looks wrong: the control renders, both segments are live, `aria-pressed` still tracks the choice and moves on every press (the state and the persistence are untouched), the rail still draws its creative, and every `getByRole`/`getByLabelText` in the suite that looks for a FIELD still finds one -- because the form never left. Only the thing the owner asked for is missing. Caught by the swap half of the fault-1 test, which reads the column's own panel marker (`data-testid="column-yaml"`) rather than searching the document for YAML text: a `screen.getByText(/targetRegion/)` would be satisfied by the projection in any column and would pass here.

mutations.because: The SAME claim from the other side, and the one the brief names as this lane's easy mistake: the control is moved onto the column and left wired to the rail, so choosing the document still takes the preview away. It is the most plausible defect in the diff, because it is what the code DID: before this lane `yaml` unmounted `PreviewDock` and put a `<pre>` in its place, so 'the YAML replaces the creative' is the behaviour a reader is carrying forward, and RS-D3 ('presence of the value is what reveals the column') makes `setRail(null)` the idiomatic way to spell it. It is two edits rather than one on purpose, and that is itself the finding: `columnView` is NOT in this effect's dependency list, so gating the body alone changes NOTHING -- the effect never re-runs, the published element is identity-stable, the shell re-renders nothing, and the switch would appear to work. The dependency has to be added for the defect to exist at all, which is why the anchor spans both. Every network proof stays green under it (a rail that is gone fetches nothing, exactly like a rail that is quiet) and so does every test that never presses `yaml`. Caught by the rail half of the fault-1 test, by a count of MOUNTS (`data-testid="preview-frame"`, present in both branches `PreviewFrame` renders): the viewport gate hides the rail without unmounting it and happy-dom applies no CSS, so a visible-node count could not tell 'the rail went' from 'the rail is narrow'. It also reddens the fault-4 flip test, where the remount pays a fresh request.

mutations.because: The projection, replaced by the editor state -- the defect the deleted Review step existed to catch (SG-D8). It is the plausible mistake for a view of 'the brief': `state` IS the editor's own object, it is the nearer name in scope, and every field the operator typed is in it. What it loses is the only thing this panel is for: `toBrief(state)` drops, trims and gates on the way out, so a value that never reached the document would be on screen as though it had. A test asserting mere PRESENCE of a field would stay green through this -- both objects carry `targetRegion`, `campaignMessage`, `products` -- and so would every other test in the file, because nothing else reads the panel's text. Caught by probing a field where the two provably DISAGREE: `toBrief` trims `localizedMessage` (`editor-state.ts`) while `CopySection` writes the raw input, so a padded `"  ja  "` is `localizedMessage: ja` in the projection and `localizedMessage: '  ja  '` in the state -- js-yaml quotes a padded string, so the two spellings cannot be confused. Both halves are asserted, the projection's present and the state's ABSENT, so the failure names a line rather than merely missing one.
command: the YAML view renders the projection, not the editor state

mutations.because: `validate` arriving before the view it shows -- SG-D13's third position wired to nothing, which is precisely the defect that cost this project two days: a surface that exists, looks live and shows nothing. It is the plausible mistake because SG-D13 is stamped and says the control has three positions, so growing the list reads as implementing a decision rather than shipping an empty segment. **This mutation is caught TWICE, by two different gates, and that is the point of the structure.** `typecheck` refuses it outright -- `COLUMN_VIEW_LABEL`, `COLUMN_VIEW_GLYPH` and `columnPanels` are each a `Record<ColumnView, ...>`, so the union cannot grow until a label, a glyph and a PANEL exist; that is the guarantee that lets SG10 add its position without reshaping anything. And because vitest does not typecheck, the runtime gate answers too: the control renders a third button whose `aria-label` is `undefined`, so it has no accessible name and no panel behind it, and the count assertion reads 3 where it requires 2. A test that merely looked for the two buttons it expects would pass on all three.
command: the switch offers exactly two positions

mutations.after: // SG1 — a reveal is a scroll and nothing else.
mutations.because: The gap this lane would otherwise have introduced, and the reason it is a gap rather than a nicety. In the `yaml` view the whole form is unmounted, so `revealSection`'s `target?.scrollIntoView` finds nothing and returns in SILENCE (`scroll-to-section.ts` -- optional chaining, no throw, no log). The action bar is not hidden by the switch, so its Save and its ErrorStrip chips stay pressable while the document is up: without this line a refused Save names a section, moves nowhere, and says nothing -- a surface that looks perfectly live. Deleting it is the plausible tidy-up, because `reveal`'s own docblock says a reveal 'is now a scroll and nothing else' (SG1 deleted W6.2's deferred half) and a view flip inside it reads as machinery that was removed on purpose. Every test that never enters the `yaml` view stays green, which is almost all of them: in `editor` the flip is React's own no-op, so the two lines below behave identically with and without it. Caught by the one test that reveals FROM `yaml`, which asserts the scroll landed on the section ELEMENT (`scroller.mock.instances`) and not merely that something scrolled -- a weaker assertion would pass on a scroll against the YAML `<pre>`, which is exactly what a flip without `flushSync` produces.
command: a reveal from the `yaml` view flips back to the editor and then scrolls
